visual.caption: Confusion, hypotension, tachycardia, low urine output, raised lactate, low albumin.
Any one means high suspicion of sepsis.
Antibiotics are the single most important treatment.

events.x: Source control: drain abscess, remove lines

glossary.Dysregulated: Out of control; the immune response becomes excessive and harms the body's own organs.
glossary.Organ dysfunction: An organ not working properly, e.g. confusion, low urine output or raised creatinine.
glossary.Fever: Raised body temperature, usually above 38°C, often a sign of infection.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Inflammatory markers: Blood tests that rise with inflammation, such as CRP and white cell count.
glossary.Systolic BP: The higher blood pressure number, measured as the heart contracts.
glossary.Fluid resuscitation: Giving IV fluids quickly to restore circulating volume and blood pressure.
glossary.Vital signs: Basic observations: heart rate, blood pressure, breathing rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, consciousness.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function, sodium and potassium.
glossary.Blood gas: Blood test for pH, oxygen, carbon dioxide, lactate, electrolytes and glucose, with results in minutes.
glossary.Electrolytes: Charged salts in blood such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.Urine culture: Growing bacteria from a urine sample to find a urinary source of infection.
glossary.Sputum culture: Growing bacteria from coughed-up phlegm to find a chest source.
glossary.Chest X-ray: Plain film of the chest, here looking for pneumonia as the source.
glossary.Urinary catheter: A tube passed into the bladder to drain and accurately measure urine output.
glossary.Hypoxic: Having low oxygen levels in the blood.
glossary.Gram-positive: Bacteria that stain purple on Gram stain, with a thick cell wall, e.g. Staphylococcus, Streptococcus.
glossary.Gram-negative: Bacteria that stain pink on Gram stain, with an outer membrane, e.g. E. coli.
glossary.Anaerobic: Organisms that grow without oxygen, common in abdominal and pelvic infections.
glossary.Adrenaline: A hormone and drug that raises heart rate, contractility and vascular tone.
glossary.Infusion: Continuous delivery of a drug through a drip or pump.
glossary.Abscess: A walled-off collection of pus that antibiotics cannot penetrate well and usually needs draining.
glossary.Microvascular dysfunction: Failure of the smallest blood vessels to deliver blood to tissues properly.
glossary.Relative hypovolaemia: Normal blood volume but too little filling the widened vessels, acting like blood loss.
glossary.Tissue oxygen delivery: Amount of oxygen carried to tissues, depending on blood flow, haemoglobin and saturation.
glossary.Vascular tone: Degree of tightening of blood vessel walls, which sets blood pressure.
glossary.0.9% saline: Normal saline: salt water with roughly the same sodium as blood, the standard resuscitation fluid.
